name: Day Job
tagline: You could make the whole room feel slow. You never have.
epigraph: Its first maker put out booklets of the bar's drinks. This one's in none of them.
language_row: Wren's Resonance (v3): horoscope, swap and punch pass; v1's "come for you or for what you can do" (the Mechanic's turn) replaced; "seemingly casual" kept out (*Not Too Polite*, *Nothing to It* and *Half a Rim* own "looks effortless"); "the other half" kept off the closing line (three Hero siblings); every he/his is Constante or Trader Vic; 4-word runs clear of the registry. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/constante-ribalaigua-floridita.md` (*Oxford Companion* RIBALAIGUA Y VERT pdf 1655–1657, FLORIDITA pdf 821, and pdf 853; Wondrich, *Imbibe!* pdf 215–216; Regan, *The Joy of Mixology* pdf 317, 412; *Cocktail Codex* p. 103; *The Flavor Matrix* pdf 80). Room notes: `work/hero-magician/`.
names_note: **Day Job**, the room's pick, 3–0 (Wren's; Tomás moved in the vote, since "every morning" is already in *The Wink* and *Whoever Comes In*; Hester: true to the page, he still went behind the bar every morning). Also considered: *Every Morning* (Tomás's lean until the vote), *Plain Clothes* (half-contradicts the reading's turn), *Not in the Booklet* (about the drink, not the person).
open_items: **The drink isn't in his booklets:** Oxford's "for reasons unknown" (pdf 821); any motive stays out of the guest text, and the reading says "for reasons we don't know".

**Trader Vic:** the Floridita survived through his menu and guide (Oxford pdf 821), and Vic is *Hold the Shark*'s man. The reading names him once and never says the recipe is his; it "starts from the Floridita, with two changes of my own".

**Two changes from the printed drink:** half a lime instead of one (Oxford's whole lime at today's yield is OUT on ABV, acid and dilution), and the lime's own peel instead of the orange twist (*Flavor Matrix* pdf 80).

**Guards:** no "Daiquiri" and never "the Floridita Daiquiri" in guest text; no Hemingway; the crown ("king of Cuban drink makers") kept out; "every morning" scoped to the late 1930s to 1950, never "until he died".
